questions.q: What did David do during his first cold night on the shore, before day began to break?
choices: Walked up and down the sand barefoot so he would not freeze
Built a small fire from bits of driftwood to dry his wet clothes
Slept curled up inside an old fisherman's hut
Sat on a rock calling out for Alan and the crew
questions.evidence: took off my shoes and walked to and fro upon the sand

questions.q: What did David see when he climbed the hill at dawn?
choices: The brig still stuck fast upon the reef
The ship's boat rowing toward the mainland
No brig, no boat, no sail and no house
A village of fishers just across the water
questions.evidence: There was no sign of the brig

questions.q: As David followed the creek around, what did he suddenly realize?
choices: That he had walked in a full circle right back to the bay
That he was on a small island cut off by the sea
That the creek led to a fresh-water spring
That the land he stood on was the Isle of Iona
questions.evidence: I was cast upon a little barren isle, and cut off on every side by the salt seas

questions.q: What happened when David first tried to wade across the creek?
choices: The water reached only to his knees
He plunged in over his head
A strong current pulled him out to sea
He cut his feet on sharp shells
questions.evidence: I plumped in head over ears

questions.q: Why did David fling himself down on the sand and weep the first time?
choices: He had found the body of one of the sailors
He saw the spare yard floating just out of his reach
He had lost the last of his money in the sea
He realized that nobody in the world knew he was still alive
questions.evidence: I saw it bobbing very quietly some twenty feet beyond

questions.q: Unlike castaways in books, what did David have in his pockets?
choices: Only his money and Alan's silver button
A knife, a flint and a bit of fishing string
His uncle's letter and a small Bible
Some bread and cheese from the brig
questions.evidence: I had nothing in my pockets but money and Alan's silver button

questions.q: What did David eat on the island?
choices: Gulls' eggs gathered from the outlying rocks
Raw limpets and buckies from the rocks
Fish he caught with a line from his stockings
Berries from the heather
questions.evidence: Of these two I made my whole diet, devouring them cold and raw

questions.q: David found "some of the little shells that we call buckies." What are buckies?
choices: Periwinkles, a kind of small shellfish
Pebbles that glitter in the sunlight
Small crabs that hide in the seaweed
Seeds that wash up on the shore
questions.evidence: I think periwinkle is the English name

questions.q: What happened after David ate his very first meal of shellfish?
choices: He felt strong enough to swim the creek
He became giddy and very sick
He fell into a long and peaceful sleep
He felt hungrier than he had before
questions.evidence: I was seized with giddiness and retching

questions.q: Why did David choose the part of the isle near the bay facing Iona as his "home"?
choices: It had the only dry cave on the whole island
He could see Iona's church and the smoke of homes
The fishers' hut there still had a good turf roof
It was the only place where the gulls did not nest
questions.evidence: I could catch a sight of the great, ancient church and the roofs of the people's houses in Iona

questions.q: How did seeing the smoke and roofs of other people's homes affect David?
choices: It made him so angry that he stopped watching for boats
It made him feel worse but also kept his hope alive
It made him certain the people there were enemies
It made him forget his hunger for a whole day

questions.q: What animal did David see on the top of the island on the third morning?
choices: A red deer buck with fine antlers
A wild goat with a broken horn
A grey seal lying on the rocks
A shaggy Highland cow
questions.evidence: I saw a red deer, a buck with a fine spread of antlers

questions.q: How had David lost most of his money?
choices: A gull snatched his purse from a rock
It slipped out through a hole in his pocket
He dropped it while wading in the creek
The sailors had stolen every coin of it on the brig
questions.evidence: I now saw there must be a hole

questions.q: David says patching his pocket then "was to lock the stable door after the steed was stolen." What does he mean?
choices: He was being careful, just in time
It was too late to do any good
He was guarding the wrong thing
He was afraid of being robbed again
questions.evidence: this was to lock the stable door after the steed was stolen

questions.q: What did the two fishers do the first time their boat passed close to David?
choices: They waved and promised to come back after dark
They threw him a loaf of bread and sailed off
They shouted in Gaelic and laughed, but sailed on
They pretended not to see him at all
questions.evidence: they cried out in the Gaelic tongue, and laughed

questions.q: When the boat came back, how did David know it was the same two fishers?
choices: By their hair, one bright yellow and one black
By the brown sail with a patch in the middle
By the Gaelic song they were always singing
By the old blue coats both of them were wearing
questions.evidence: This I knew by their hair

questions.q: What did David do after he understood the word "tide"?
choices: He swam out to the fishers' boat
He ran across the isle and waded the creek
He waited on his rock for the tide to come in
He asked the third man to row him to Iona
questions.evidence: set off running across the isle as I had never run before

questions.q: What is the big lesson David draws from his days on Earraid?
choices: That fishers in the Highlands are cruel to strangers
That the isle was tidal, and he suffered from his own folly
That a castaway should always carry a set of tools in his pockets
That he should never again go to sea in any ship
questions.evidence: I might have left my bones there, in pure folly
